# 1. Descriptive epidemiology

## Text

> Between 2022 and 2024, `r fmt_n(desc_numbers$n_total)` residents of the ATS Milano
> territory died before the age of 75 from causes considered avoidable, a median
> of `r fmt_n(desc_numbers$n_per_year, 0)` deaths per year, with a median age at death of
> `r fmt_num(desc_numbers$median_age, 0)` years
> (IQR `r fmt_num(desc_numbers$iqr_low, 0)`–`r fmt_num(desc_numbers$iqr_high, 0)`).
> Of these, `r fmt_n(desc_numbers$n_preventable)` (`r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$pct_preventable)`)
> were at least partially preventable and
> `r fmt_n(desc_numbers$n_treatable)` (`r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$pct_treatable)`) at least
> partially amenable to treatment; the two categories overlap because
> `r fmt_n(desc_numbers$n_both)` deaths (`r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$pct_both)`) arose from one of
> the seven causes the classification splits equally between the two lists.
> Men accounted for `r fmt_n(desc_numbers$n_men)` (`r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$pct_men)`) of
> avoidable deaths and women for `r fmt_n(desc_numbers$n_women)`
> (`r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$pct_women)`).
>
> Most avoidable deaths were related to cancer
> (`r fmt_n(desc_numbers$cancer$n)`, `r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$cancer$pct)`), diseases of the
> circulatory system (`r fmt_n(desc_numbers$circulatory$n)`,
> `r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$circulatory$pct)`), and infectious diseases
> (`r fmt_n(desc_numbers$infectious$n)`, `r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$infectious$pct)`).
> The `r nrow(desc_numbers$top_causes)` leading individual causes together account for
> `r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$pct_top_causes)` of all avoidable deaths:
> `r top_causes_sentence(desc_numbers$top_causes)`.
> Environment and safety (`r fmt_n(desc_numbers$environment$n)`,
> `r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$environment$pct)`) comprises occupational respiratory disease
> but not traumatic injuries, and mental health and substance use
> (`r fmt_n(desc_numbers$mental_health$n)`, `r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$mental_health$pct)`)
> comprises alcohol- and drug-related conditions but not self-harm, since deaths
> from external causes are not part of the ReNCaM register.
>
> Grouped by the mechanism that could have averted the death, most could have
> been avoided by lifestyle and behavioural factors
> (`r fmt_n(desc_numbers$lifestyle$n)`, `r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$lifestyle$pct)`, preventable),
> by better clinical management of complications
> (`r fmt_n(desc_numbers$tertiary$n)`, `r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$tertiary$pct)`, treatable), and
> by screening programmes (`r fmt_n(desc_numbers$screening$n)`,
> `r fmt_pct(desc_numbers$screening$pct)`, treatable). The remaining four mechanisms
> account for a minority of deaths, and their small-area models have
> correspondingly wide intervals; all seven are nonetheless fitted and reported.
> Half counts reflect the weight-splitting described in the methods.

::: {.callout-note}
`n_preventable` + `n_treatable` deliberately exceeds `n_total`. The
`avoidability` table below is the mutually exclusive version and does sum to
100%.
:::

```{r avoidability}
desc_numbers$avoidability |>
  mutate(pct = fmt_pct(pct)) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Avoidability category", "Deaths", "%"),
        caption = "Mutually exclusive avoidability categories.")
```

# 2. Covariate distribution and spatial structure

## Text

> The study area comprises `r study_area_summary$n_areas` areal units —
> `r study_area_summary$n_comuni` municipalities and the
> `r study_area_summary$n_nil` Local Identity Units into which the municipality
> of Milan is disaggregated — covering a mean annual resident population of
> `r fmt_n(study_area_summary$mean_annual_population)`.
>
> Crude mortality rates ranged from `r rng_col(crude_geo, "total", 1)` deaths per 100,000 person-years. Standardised
> mortality ratios ranged from `r rng(covariate_table, "Standardised mortality ratio")`.
> Expected counts averaged `r mean_of(covariate_table, "Expected deaths")`
> deaths per areal unit over the three-year period, with a range of
> `r rng(covariate_table, "Expected deaths")`.
> Moran's I on the crude standardised ratios was
> `r fmt_num(moran_crude$statistic, 3)`
> (`r fmt_p(moran_crude$p_value)`, `r fmt_n(moran_crude$n_sim)` permutations),
> indicating that risk in neighbouring areas was more similar than risk in
> distant areas and supporting a specification incorporating spatially
> structured variation.
>
> The Italian Deprivation Index ranged from
> `r rng(covariate_table, "Deprivation Index")` in summed z-score units, with a
> median of `r median_of(covariate_table, "Deprivation Index")`, which sits
> below the national average of zero: the ATS Milano territory is among the more
> affluent in the country.
>
> Nitrogen dioxide averaged `r mean_of(covariate_table, "NO2 (ug/m3)")` µg/m³
> (SD `r sd_of(covariate_table, "NO2 (ug/m3)")`), while PM2.5 averaged
> `r mean_of(covariate_table, "PM2.5 (ug/m3)")` µg/m³
> (SD `r sd_of(covariate_table, "PM2.5 (ug/m3)")`), showing markedly less
> contrast across the study area. NO₂ was therefore selected as the primary
> environmental exposure. The two pollutants correlate at
> `r fmt_num(cor_between(covariate_correlations, "no2", "pm25"), 2)` (Spearman),
> which is why they are mutually attenuating when entered jointly and are
> instead compared across M5 and M7.
>
> The testable implication of the DAG — that primary care capacity is
> conditionally independent of the outcome given deprivation and location — was
> assessed by correlating M4's residuals with primary care capacity. The
> correlation was `r fmt_num(cond_independence$estimate, 3)`
> (`r fmt_p(cond_independence$p_value)`), so the implication
> `r ifelse(cond_independence$p_value > 0.05, "was not contradicted", "was contradicted")`.
> Note that surviving one testable implication is weak evidence for a graph;
> failing one would have been strong evidence against it.

# 3. Model comparison

## Text

> `r convergence_sentence(model_diagnostics)`
>
> The comparison by approximate leave-one-out cross-validation is shown in
> Table 3. `r loo_sentence(tbl_loo)`
> `r pareto_sentence(pareto_audit, "M5")`
> Moran's I on M5 residuals was `r by_model(moran_residual, "M5", "statistic")`
> (`r by_model(moran_residual, "M5", "p_value", fmt = fmt_p)`), indicating
> the spatial component
> `r moran_verdict(moran_residual, "M5")`
> absorbed the structure present in the crude ratios.

```{r diagnostics-table}
model_diagnostics |>
  mutate(across(c(rhat_max, ebfmi_min, rho), \(x) fmt_num(x, 3)),
         across(c(ess_min, n_divergent, treedepth_hits), \(x) fmt_n(x)),
         pct_divergent = fmt_pct(pct_divergent),
         waic = fmt_num(waic, 1)) |>
  select(model, n_draws, rhat_max, ess_min, n_divergent, pct_divergent,
         treedepth_hits, ebfmi_min, rho, waic) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Model", "Draws", "Max R-hat", "Min ESS", "Divergent",
                      "% divergent", "Treedepth hits", "Min E-BFMI", "rho",
                      "WAIC"),
        caption = "Convergence and sampler diagnostics, M1–M7.")
```

```{r loo-table}
tbl_loo |>
  mutate(across(c(elpd_loo, se_elpd, p_loo, looic, elpd_diff, se_diff),
                \(x) fmt_num(x, 1)),
         ratio = fmt_num(ratio, 1)) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Model", "elpd LOO", "SE", "p_loo", "LOOIC",
                      "elpd diff", "SE diff", "|diff|/SE", "Verdict",
                      "Pareto-k > 0.7"),
        caption = "Leave-one-out comparison, ordered best first. Higher elpd is better.")
```

```{r moran-table}
moran_residual |>
  mutate(across(c(statistic, post_mean, post_low, post_high), \(x) fmt_num(x, 3)),
         p_value = fmt_p(p_value)) |>
  select(model, statistic, p_value, post_mean, post_low, post_high) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Model", "Moran's I", "p", "Posterior mean I",
                      "2.5%", "97.5%"),
        caption = "Moran's I on Pearson residuals. Computed on residuals, not on smoothed relative risks — the latter are spatially autocorrelated by construction.")
```

```{r pareto-table}
if (nrow(pareto_audit)) {
  pareto_audit |>
    mutate(across(c(pareto_k, expected, population), \(x) fmt_num(x, 2))) |>
    kable(caption = "Areas where the leave-one-out approximation is unreliable under M5, ordered by expected count.")
} else {
  cat("No area exceeded a Pareto-k of 0.7 under M5.\n")
}
```

# 4. Avoidable mortality estimates and risk surface

## 4.1 Residual excess

> Summed across the study area, `r fmt_num(excess$total$excess_per_year, 0)`
> deaths per year occurred beyond what age and sex structure, deprivation, air
> pollution and primary care capacity jointly predict (95% credible interval
> `r fmt_num(excess$total$ci_low, 0)` to `r fmt_num(excess$total$ci_high, 0)`),
> which is `r fmt_pct(excess$total$pct_of_total)` of overall avoidable
> mortality. Adding the covariates to the unadjusted model reduced between-area
> variance by `r fmt_pct(variance_reduction$reduction$pct_reduction)`
> (95% CrI `r fmt_pct(variance_reduction$reduction$ci_low)` to
> `r fmt_pct(variance_reduction$reduction$ci_high)`), so the measured
> determinants account for
> `r ifelse(variance_reduction$reduction$pct_reduction < 50, "rather less than half", "most")`
> of the geographical variation in avoidable death.
>
> `r excess$n_flagged` areas had a posterior probability above
> `r excess$prob_cutoff` that their residual relative risk exceeded
> `r excess$threshold`.

```{r variance-table}
variance_reduction$by_model |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) fmt_num(x, 3))) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Model", "Residual variance", "2.5%", "97.5%",
                      "Residual SD", "2.5%", "97.5%", "rho"),
        caption = "Between-area residual variation before and after adjustment.")
```

```{r excess-flagged-table}
excess$per_area |>
  filter(flagged) |>
  arrange(desc(excess)) |>
  mutate(across(c(excess, excess_low, excess_high, rr_resid), \(x) fmt_num(x, 2)),
         p_exceed = fmt_num(p_exceed, 2)) |>
  select(area, observed, expected, excess, excess_low, excess_high,
         rr_resid, p_exceed) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Area", "Observed", "Expected", "Excess/yr", "2.5%",
                      "97.5%", "Residual RR", "P(RR > 1.20)"),
        caption = "Areas flagged as showing residual excess under M5.")
```

```{r fig-excess, fig.cap="Residual excess avoidable deaths per year under M5."}
fig_excess_map
```

```{r fig-excess-flagged, fig.cap="Residual excess, restricted to areas exceeding the 0.80 probability cutoff."}
fig_excess_flagged
```

## 4.2 Risk surface

> Smoothed relative risks ranged from `r rr_range(aug_M3)` (Figure 4.3), a
> considerably narrower range than the standardised mortality ratios.
> At the `r 0.80` probability cutoff, `r n_exceeding(aug_M3, 0.80)` areas were
> classified as showing excess. The remaining areas are not evidence of evenly
> distributed risk; they reflect the model's expected behaviour given lower
> counts, which produce broader posteriors.

::: {.callout-important}
The draft names two clusters — "the Magenta–Legnano axis" and "the Lodi
extension". Check them against the flagged-area table above before keeping
those sentences. They were written from an earlier run and are not currently
generated from the data.
:::

```{r fig-rr, fig.cap="BYM2-smoothed relative risk, M3 (no covariates)."}
fig_rr_map
```

```{r fig-exceedance, fig.cap="Exceedance probability that relative risk exceeds 1.20, M3."}
fig_exceedance
```

## 4.3 Sensitivity to specifications

> The eigenvector spatial filtering specification (M6) and the BYM2
> specification (M5) rank areas at a Spearman correlation of
> `r fmt_num(surface_cor(aug_M5, aug_M6), 3)`. `r esf_verdict(aug_M5, aug_M6)`


```{r sensitivity-coefs}
sensitivity_coefficients |>

  select(model, label, estimate, ci_low, ci_high) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Model", "Term", "RR", "2.5%", "97.5%"),
```

# 5. Avoidable mortality by mechanism

```{r mechanism-table}

                \(x) fmt_num(x, 2))) |>

         rr_min, rr_max, n_exceed) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Service function", "Deaths", "rho", "2.5%", "97.5%",
```

```{r mechanism-diagnostics}
  select(model, rhat_max, ess_min, n_divergent, pct_divergent, ebfmi_min) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Service function", "Max R-hat", "Min ESS", "Divergent",
```

> `r stroke_time_sentence(stroke_times_table)`
>
> `r control_sentence(control_table)`

been chosen. The panel below therefore has three of its four slots filled. See
the work log for two candidate exposures.

```{r stroke-times}
stroke_times_table |>
```
